overview: Compton Bay is a two-mile sweep of golden and dark sand on the Isle of Wight's south-west coast, between Freshwater Bay and Brook, under the chalk ridge of Compton Down. The National Trust looks after the bay, the downs and the three car parks along the Military Road. The sea stays shallow a long way out, and the soft cliffs behind are always crumbling onto the beach.

It's known for fossils as much as surf. The rocks are Cretaceous, around 130 million years old, and the shore gives up dinosaur bones, fossilised wood and footprints in the sandstone ledge at Hanover Point, which show at low tide. The National Trust runs guided fossil walks on set dates, and the Isle of Wight Coast Path and the Round the Island cycle route both run along the top.

For surfers it's the island's most reliable beach. It faces into the prevailing south-westerly swell, and three separate set-ups along the bay mean there is usually somewhere that works. It's a genuinely exposed spot rather than a gentle learner's beach, there are no lifeguards, and summer is often flat. Come in autumn or winter for the best of it.

text: Compton is a long beach break with three main set-ups, all giving lefts and rights over sand with a flat rocky reef partly buried beneath. Fields, at the northern end, is the consistent one, with good peaks around mid-tide in a medium swell. Middle Compton, further along, is more flexible and tends to have the most powerful peaks. Hanover Point, at the southern end, is a mellower A-frame that works best in a medium swell from mid to high tide, and it's the section that draws the biggest crowd.

The classic combination is a south-westerly swell with a north-easterly wind blowing off the land, and a rising tide between mid and high water is the one to aim for. It works from around waist-high up to well overhead, though it gets more serious and much harder to read as the swell builds. Waves can break a long way out, so expect a proper paddle, and when it's big the water gets rippy.

Season matters here. Autumn, especially September to November, is the sweet spot, with winter bringing the biggest and most reliable swells. Summer is mostly flat, so don't plan a surf trip around July. On the rare days when a long-period swell meets offshore wind, locals turn up in numbers and spectators line the beach to watch.

The lineup is usually friendly, but the same etiquette applies as anywhere: give priority to whoever is furthest inside, don't drop in, and expect more people at Hanover Point than elsewhere. Nearly any board works, from shortboards and fish to funboards, longboards, SUPs and bodyboards, but there is no lifeguard cover, so be honest about your ability.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Intermediate
cards.text: Better for improvers and up. Beginners should go with a school, on a small day, at Hanover Point.

cards.label: Hazards
cards.title: Reef, rips and cliffs
cards.text: Rocks under the sand, rips and a long paddle when it's big, and eroding cliffs: don't sit or change under them.

cards.label: Season
cards.title: Autumn into winter
cards.text: September to November is best; winter is biggest. Summer is usually flat and much busier.

cards.label: Boards
cards.title: Almost anything
cards.text: Shortboards, fish, funboards, longboards, SUPs and bodyboards all work on the right day.

practical.label: Parking
practical.title: Three National Trust car parks
practical.text: Brook, Hanover Point and Compton Bay (Compton Chine) are pay and display through the JustPark app; free for National Trust members who register their card there. No overnight or coach parking, and the Military Road is a clearway, so don't park on the verges: you'll get a penalty notice.

practical.label: Access
practical.title: Steep steps at every route
practical.text: Hanover Point and Compton both have steep, tiered wooden steps down to the sand, and Brook has steps too. Plan on carrying your board down and back up, and don't climb the cliffs instead.

practical.label: Facilities
practical.title: Hanover Point only
practical.text: Toilets with baby change and a Changing Places cubicle at the Hanover Point car park. A catering van runs in summer, about five days a week; outside that, bring your own food and drink, as there's nothing else on the beach.

practical.label: Tides
practical.title: Check before you go
practical.text: Tides change the beach a lot and can cut off access along the foot of the cliffs, so check times before walking along the bay. Low tide is when the dinosaur footprints at Hanover Point show.

practical.label: Dogs
practical.title: Seasonal
practical.text: Dogs are welcome all year between Hanover Point and Brook Chine; banned west of Compton Bay car park 15 May to 15 September.

practical.label: Getting here
practical.title: Lymington–Yarmouth ferry
practical.text: The shortest car crossing for this coast. A Southern Vectis bus runs from Newport to Compton Bay in summer only.

faqs.q: Is Compton Bay good for surfing?
faqs.a: It's the Isle of Wight's most consistent surf beach. It faces the prevailing south-westerly swell and works best on a rising tide between mid and high water, with a north-easterly offshore wind. Autumn and winter are best; summer is mostly flat.

faqs.q: Is Compton Bay good for beginners?
faqs.a: Not on its own. It's an exposed beach with rocks under the sand, rips when it's big and no lifeguards. Beginners should go with a school on a small day; Hanover Point is the mellowest section.

faqs.q: Where should I surf at Compton Bay?
faqs.a: Fields at the northern end is the consistent beach break, Middle Compton has the more powerful peaks, and Hanover Point at the southern end is the mellow, busier A-frame.

faqs.q: How do you pay for parking?
faqs.a: Through the JustPark app; National Trust members park free once registered. In summer you can also pay at the catering van.

faqs.q: Can I leave my van overnight?
faqs.a: No. Overnight parking isn't allowed at any of the car parks, and parking on the Military Road verges is prohibited.

faqs.q: Can dogs go on Compton Bay?
faqs.a: Yes, between Hanover Point and Brook Chine all year. West of the Compton car park, dogs are banned from 15 May to 15 September.
